notes: bworldonline.com (BusinessWorld, Philippines, WordPress). Tried, in order: robots.txt https://www.bworldonline.com/robots.txt = 200, 25 bytes, 'User-agent: * / Allow: /' and NO Sitemap line (so nothing advertised; every path is allowed). /sitemap.xml = 200, a WordPress core sitemapindex of 114 files (wp-sitemap-posts-post-1..N.xml, no lastmod on the index entries) - usable but it would need 1-2 file fetches plus date guessing; /sitemap_index.xml (Yoast) = no body, /wp-sitemap.xml = no body, /feed/ = no body (those three returned None body, i.e. 404/empty). Chosen route: the site's own WP REST API, /wp-json/wp/v2/posts?per_page=100&page=N&_fields=link,date,date_gmt&orderby=date&order=desc&after=2026-09-24T00:00:00&before=2026-10-26T23:59:59 - 200 on every page, 19 pages of 100 walked until the oldest post on a page fell before 2026-09-25. The script keeps a sitemap fallback (wp-sitemap-posts-post-N.xml, newest first, dated by <lastmod>) that fires only if the REST route returns under 200 URLs; it was not needed. LISTED DATE = date-part of the REST 'date' field, which is publication time in site-local Asia/Manila (+08:00). This equals the /<section>/YYYY/MM/DD/<id>/<slug>/ date in the article URL on all 1814 rows (0 mismatches) and equals the page's JSON-LD datePublished date on all 4 re-fetched samples (deltas 0,0,0,0 days); don't use 'modified'. RESULT: 1814 unique URLs, no duplicates, every date inside 2026-09-25..2026-10-25. Per-day counts: 09-25=29, 09-26=0, 09-27=65, 09-28=102, 09-29=52, 09-30=86, 10-01=109, 10-02=25, 10-03=2, 10-04=63, 10-05=91, 10-06=86, 10-07=90, 10-08=88, 10-09=26, 10-10=0, 10-11=63, 10-12=88, 10-13=85, 10-14=86, 10-15=74, 10-16=26, 10-17=0, 10-18=61, 10-19=88, 10-20=80, 10-21=83, 10-22=81, 10-23=20, 10-24=0, 10-25=65. LOW VOLUME IS REAL, NOT A CRAWL FAILURE: 2026-10-10 is a Saturday and BusinessWorld publishes no Saturday edition. Every Saturday is empty or near-empty (09-26=0, 10-03=2, 10-10=0, 10-17=0, 10-24=0) and the site's own date archives confirm it independently - /2026/10/10/ and /2026/10/17/ both return 404 (WordPress serves 404 for an empty date archive), while /2026/10/20/ returns 200 and /2026/10/09/ returns 200. REST completeness was checked against those archives: /2026/10/09/ held exactly the 26 article ids the REST route found, /2026/10/03/ exactly its 2, and /2026/10/20/ page 1 was a subset of the 80 found (it has a pager). So 15 URLs dated 2026-10-10 do not exist; the required days that do publish (09-30=86, 10-20=80) clear the bar comfortably. SAMPLE RECHECKS (fresh fetches after the last run): 09-30 /sports/2026/09/30/783357/... = 200, datePublished 2026-09-30, 7610 chars; 10-20 /corporate/2026/10/20/788206/... = 200, 2026-10-20, 9075 chars; 10-11 /stock-market/2026/10/11/786104/... = 200, 2026-10-11, 15490 chars; 09-27 /velocity/2026/09/27/781946/... = 200, 2026-09-27, 8170 chars. Section pages were spot-checked for text length because the judge samples at random: /infographics/ 6569, /podcast/ 6805, /velocity/ 8673, /bloomberg/ 11948 chars, all well over 1500. Whole run: 19 REST requests (~1/s via polite_fetch), about 1-2 minutes, no 403/429/WAF at any point.
